title: SRB-induced peptidomic profiling of Hermetia illucens larvae for antimicrobial peptide discovery
projectDescription: eptidomic profiling was performed to identify antimicrobial peptides induced in fifth-instar Hermetia illucens larvae following challenge with the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris. Larvae challenged with D. vulgaris were compared with untreated controls. Differentially abundant peptides were identified, and upregulated candidates were further screened using antimicrobial peptide prediction and database analysis. Four candidate peptides (DH-1–DH-4) were selected for subsequent experimental evaluation, leading to the identification of DH-1 as the lead candidate.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Fifth-instar Hermetia illucens larvae were divided into Desulfovibrio vulgaris-challenged and untreated control groups. Larvae in the challenged group were injected with 20 μL of D. vulgaris suspension and collected 24 h after challenge. Surviving larvae without visible melanization were flash-frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at −80 °C. Samples were ground under liquid nitrogen and lysed in 8 M urea containing 1% protease inhibitor. Following sonication and centrifugation, the supernatants were subjected to ultrafiltration to collect peptide-containing filtrates. Peptides were separated using an EASY-nLC 1200 system and analyzed by tandem mass spectrometry.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw LC-MS/MS data were processed using MaxQuant version 1.6.15.0 and searched against a Hermetia illucens protein sequence database (Blast_Hermetia_illucens_343691_PR_20231012.fasta). Peptide identification was performed using an unspecific search with peptide lengths of 8–25 amino acids and no fixed modifications. Oxidation (M) and protein N-terminal acetylation were specified as variable modifications. The main search precursor mass tolerance was 4.5 ppm, and the FTMS MS/MS fragment mass tolerance was 20 ppm. The peptide-spectrum match and peptide false discovery rates were set to 1%. Match between runs was enabled with a matching time window of 0.7 min. Label-free peptide intensities were used for comparison between the D. vulgaris-challenged and untreated control samples.
